Capital expenditures in investing activities are based on ending gross fixed asset balances ($183,956.52 shop assets + $122,389.98 leasehold improvements) due to absence of prior-period fixed asset balances. Actual 2025 additions may be materially lower if assets were acquired in prior periods. General Ledger detail is required to isolate current-year additions.

Account 4012 Woodworking Gift-In-Kind Income ($4,589.67) is treated as a non-cash revenue item and deducted from net income in operating activities. If any portion was received as cash, this adjustment should be revised.

Account 1002 Northwestern Mutual Investment Services ($317,374.28) is classified under Bank Accounts in QuickBooks and included in ending cash. If this account does not meet the GAAP definition of cash equivalents (original maturity of 3 months or less), it should be reclassified to investing activities and excluded from the cash reconciliation ending balance.

partI_summary.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, skill development, and community engagement. The Guild provides members with access to a fully equipped woodworking shop, educational classes, safety training, and program events that advance woodworking knowledge and craftsmanship.

partIII_programServiceAccomplishments.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, skill development, and community engagement. The Guild provides members with access to a fully equipped woodworking shop, educational classes, safety training, and program events that advance woodworking knowledge and craftsmanship.

programServices.description: Membership Program: The Guild provided members with access to a fully equipped woodworking shop facility located at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO. Membership dues support ongoing shop operations, equipment maintenance, and member benefits including shop access, storage, and use of tools and machinery. The Guild collected $171,525 in membership dues revenue and incurred $150,000 in facility rent expense to maintain the shop space available to members throughout the year.

Woodworking Skills Education: The Guild offered a comprehensive curriculum of woodworking skills classes and workshops, including Rough to Ready introductory courses, intermediate woodworking, bandsaw box, project finishing, hand tool woodworking, and other skill-building classes. Classes were conducted at the Guild's shop facility and through WildApricot event registration. Total skills education revenue was $50,217 and program expenses were $38,495, including instructor costs and merchant processing fees of $2,955.

Woodworking Program Events: The Guild organized and hosted woodworking program events and special events for members and the public, including special interest group (SIG) meetings covering CNC, carving, finishing, hand tools, laser engraving, and other woodworking disciplines, as well as monthly membership meetings and community events such as the National Craft Open Studios Weekend. Total program events revenue was $7,995 and expenses were $12,567, including special events expense of $10,009.

Other program services including: Woodworking Safety Education ($5,800 revenue / $2,902 expense) providing safety training and orientation for shop users; Woodworking Rent Income ($26,016 revenue) from subletting portions of the facility; Woodworking Storage Income ($7,232 revenue / included in occupancy) from member storage rentals; Woodworking Merchandise ($2,805 revenue / $4,841 expense); Woodworking Library ($176 revenue / $96 expense); Woodworking Assets Sold ($2,783 revenue / $2,783 expense); Woodworking Other Program Income ($5,267 revenue); Woodworking Membership Expense ($5,570); Depreciation ($32,378); Insurance ($9,474); Shop Equipment ($2,240); Shop Equipment Maintenance ($6,013); Shop Facilities Maintenance ($9,576); Shop Supplies ($5,315); Newsletter ($2,305); Trash Service ($1,800); Internet & Website ($1,318); Alarm Monitoring ($787); Program Software ($258); A/V Equipment ($709).

partI_publicCharityStatus.description: An organization that normally receives a substantial part of its support from a governmental unit or from the general public described in section 170(b)(1)(A)(vi). The organization is a publicly supported organization under section 509(a)(1) and 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) as a membership-based woodworking guild receiving substantial public support through membership dues, contributions, and program service revenue from a broad base of members and the general public.

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization incorporated in Missouri in 1992. The Guild's mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking through education, skill development, and community engagement. The Guild provides members with access to a fully equipped woodworking shop facility, offers educational classes in woodworking skills and safety, hosts program events and special interest group meetings, and fosters a community of woodworking enthusiasts in the Kansas City metropolitan area. The Guild operates from its shop located at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108, and manages its membership and event registration through WildApricot.

The organization relies extensively on volunteers to operate its woodworking shop, teach classes, lead special interest groups, organize events, and manage day-to-day operations. The number of volunteers is not tracked in the organization's accounting system; the organization estimates it utilizes volunteers throughout the year but cannot provide a precise count from available data.

Membership Program: The Guild maintained a fully equipped woodworking shop facility at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO throughout 2025. Members paid annual dues providing access to the shop, tools, equipment, and member benefits. The Guild collected $171,525 in membership dues revenue. The primary program expense was $150,000 in facility rent to maintain the shop space. Membership administration expenses including merchant processing fees totaled $5,570. The Guild also collected $26,016 in rent income from subleasing portions of the facility and $7,232 in storage income from member storage rentals.

Woodworking Skills Education: The Guild offered a broad curriculum of woodworking skills classes during 2025, including Rough to Ready introductory woodworking courses taught by multiple instructors, intermediate woodworking, bandsaw box making, project finishing, hand tool woodworking, CNC operation, laser engraving, carving, and other skill-building workshops. Classes were held at the Guild's shop facility and managed through the WildApricot membership management platform. Total skills education revenue was $50,217 and program expenses were $38,495, which included instructor compensation, materials, and merchant processing fees of $2,955.

Woodworking Program Events: The Guild organized and hosted regular program events for members and the public during 2025, including monthly membership meetings, special interest group (SIG) meetings covering CNC, carving, finishing, hand tools, laser engraving, and other woodworking disciplines, and community events such as the National Craft Open Studios Weekend. Total program events revenue was $7,995 and expenses were $12,567, including special events expense of $10,009 for the 50031 Woodworking Program Special Events sub-account.

The organization holds amounts on behalf of KC Woodturners, a related woodworking organization that shares the Guild's facility. As of December 31, 2025, the Guild held $2,197.36 in membership dues collected on behalf of KC Woodturners (account 2200 Membership Dues Payable - KC Woodturners) and $1,500.00 as a lease deposit payable to KC Woodturners (account 2201 Lease Deposit Payable - KC Woodturners), totaling $3,697.36 reported on Part X, line 21.

The organization reports land, buildings, and equipment on Part X, line 10. As of December 31, 2025, gross fixed assets totaled $306,346.50, consisting of Woodworking Shop Assets (account 1300) of $183,956.52 and Leasehold Improvements (account 1310) of $122,389.98. Accumulated depreciation totaled $193,374.13, consisting of accumulated depreciation on shop assets (account 1400) of $160,065.84 and accumulated depreciation on leasehold improvements (account 1410) of $33,308.29. Net book value of fixed assets was $112,972.37. Depreciation expense for the year was $32,377.75 ($14,853.55 on shop assets and $17,524.20 on leasehold improvements).

The organization conducted fundraising activities during 2025 through its Fundraising Projects Income account (4101), generating $61,178.50 in fundraising revenue. Fundraising project expenses (account 5101) were $27,910.08. The organization also received $2,200.00 in sponsor income (account 4013) and $4,589.67 in gift-in-kind income (account 4012). Total contributions and fundraising income exceeded $15,000. Schedule B is required.

The Form 990 is reviewed by the organization's Treasurer prior to filing. The completed return is provided to the Board of Directors for review and approval before submission to the IRS. Board members have the opportunity to ask questions and request changes before the return is filed.

The organization makes its governing documents, conflict of interest policy, and financial statements available to the public upon written request submitted to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121. The organization's Form 990 is also made available on the organization's website at www.kcwg.org. The organization does not charge a fee for providing copies of these documents.

The beginning of year net assets reported on Part XI, line 4 is $0.00 because prior year QuickBooks balance sheet data was not available to populate the beginning of year column. The organization's QuickBooks equity as of December 31, 2025 includes Opening Balance Equity of $312,303.13 and Retained Earnings of $95,091.80 representing accumulated net assets from prior years, totaling $407,394.93 reported as a prior period adjustment on line 8 to reconcile to the ending net assets of $452,353.93. The organization should obtain prior year Form 990 or prior year balance sheet to properly report beginning of year net assets in future filings.

The organization's financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 were not compiled, reviewed, or audited by an independent accountant. The financial statements were prepared internally using QuickBooks accounting software on the accrual basis of accounting.

The organization is a publicly supported organization under sections 509(a)(1) and 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) as a membership-based woodworking guild that receives substantial support from its members and the general public. The five-year support schedule reflects only the current tax year (2025) as prior year data was not available from the provided QuickBooks records. Prior year support data should be obtained from previously filed Forms 990 to complete the full five-year public support calculation. For 2025, gifts, grants, contributions, and membership fees totaled $239,503.17 (contributions $67,978.17 plus membership dues $171,525.00). The organization believes it meets the public support test but cannot confirm the percentage without prior year data.

The organization conducted raffle activities during 2025 as part of its woodworking program. Raffle sales (account 4007) totaled $2,548.00 and raffle expenses (account 5006) totaled $830.00. The raffles were conducted as part of the organization's program activities for members. The organization should consult with its tax advisor regarding any applicable federal excise tax filing requirements under section 4421 for wagering activities.
